knowledge:
- key_parameters: path=Path to the summary statistics file, or a direct dataframe/datatable ;; ref_genome=The genome build of the input GWAS ("GRCh37" or "GRCh38"); if NULL, it is inferred ;; convert_ref_genome=The target genome build to lift over to ("GRCh37" or "GRCh38") ;; save_path=The file path to save the formatted output; defaults to tempdir() which deletes files after the R session ;; return_data=Logical, if TRUE returns R objects (data.table, GRanges, VRanges) instead of saving to disk ;; return_format=The class of R object to return ("data.table", "vranges", "granges") ;; write_vcf=Logical, whether to write the output as a VCF file instead of a tabular file ;; save_format=Output format requirements, such as "ldsc" (reverses A1/A2 naming to match LDSC) or "opengwas" (IEU OpenGWAS VCF format) ;; log_folder_ind=Logical, whether to store separate log files for each class of filtered-out SNPs ;; imputation_ind=Logical, whether to add columns indicating which fields (like alleles or Z-scores) were imputed or flipped ;; nThread=Number of threads to use for parallel processes in data.table
- alternatives: ieugwasr=R interface to the IEU GWAS database API, preferred for direct programmatic access to open-access online datasets ;; gwasvcf=Package for handling GWAS VCF files, preferred if only working with VCF formats without standardisation to older tabular formats ;; vcfR=Package for parsing VCF files, but lacks automated standardisation and QC pipelines
- when_to_use: Use this package when you have raw, non-standardised GWAS summary statistics (local files or from Open GWAS) and need to clean, QC, and standardise them for downstream analyses like Linkage Disequilibrium Score Regression (LDSC) or MAGMA.
- pitfalls: By default, formatted results are saved to tempdir() and will be deleted when the R session ends unless save_path is explicitly changed or files are copied ;; If save_format="ldsc" is used, the naming convention of A1 (reference) and A2 (effect) is reversed to match LDSC (A1 becomes the effect allele), and effect columns (like Z) will be relative to A1 ;; Imputing Z-scores or sample sizes (N) for every SNP is an approximation and should only be done as a last resort ;; The reference dataset (dbSNP) does not include indels, so checks/imputations cannot be performed on indels (they may be excluded or kept without checks depending on parameters) ;; IEU OpenGWAS sumstats are currently GRCh37; saving as "openGWAS" format when data is not GRCh37 will throw a warning.

workflows.name: standardise_and_qc_gwas
workflows.intent: Standardise column headers and perform comprehensive quality control checks on local tabular or VCF GWAS summary statistics.
input: ALSvcf.vcf (VCF format GWAS summary statistics file)
workflows.stages:
1. Define the path to the raw summary statistics file.
2. Run format_sumstats() specifying the reference genome and output parameters.
3. (Optional) Run format_sumstats() with logging and imputation indicators enabled.
workflows.code:
eduAttainOkbayPth <- system.file("extdata","eduAttainOkbay.txt", package="MungeSumstats")
reformatted <- MungeSumstats::format_sumstats(path=eduAttainOkbayPth, ref_genome="GRCh37")
ALSvcfPth <- system.file("extdata","ALSvcf.vcf", package="MungeSumstats")
reformatted_vcf <- MungeSumstats::format_sumstats(path=ALSvcfPth, ref_genome="GRCh37")
reformatted_vcf_2 <- MungeSumstats::format_sumstats(path=ALSvcfPth, ref_genome="GRCh37", log_folder_ind=TRUE, imputation_ind=TRUE, log_mungesumstats_msgs=TRUE)

workflows.name: import_open_gwas
workflows.intent: Search for and import standardised GWAS summary statistics directly from the MRC IEU Open GWAS Project.
input: OPENGWAS_JWT (API token configured in the user's .Renviron file)
workflows.stages:
1. Search for datasets of interest using find_sumstats() with trait and sample size filters.
2. Import and format the selected datasets using import_sumstats().
workflows.code:
metagwas <- MungeSumstats::find_sumstats(traits = c("parkinson","alzheimer"), min_sample_size = 1000)
ids <- (dplyr::arrange(metagwas, nsnp))$id
datasets <- MungeSumstats::import_sumstats(ids = "ieu-a-298", ref_genome = "GRCH37")

workflows.name: liftover_genome_build
workflows.intent: Perform genome build liftover (e.g., hg19 to hg38) on a summary statistics data.table.
input: sumstats_dt (a data.table containing formatted GWAS summary statistics)
workflows.stages:
1. Load or format the summary statistics.
2. Run liftover() specifying the source and target genome builds.
workflows.code:
sumstats_dt <- MungeSumstats::formatted_example()
sumstats_dt_hg38 <- MungeSumstats::liftover(sumstats_dt = sumstats_dt, ref_genome = "hg19", convert_ref_genome = "hg38")

workflows.name: quick_format_from_disk
workflows.intent: Quickly standardise column headers and convert file formats without running the full QC pipeline.
workflows.stages:
1. Read the summary statistics and standardise headers using read_sumstats().
2. Write the standardised data to disk as a compressed, tabix-indexed file using write_sumstats().
workflows.code:
eduAttainOkbayPth <- system.file("extdata", "eduAttainOkbay.txt", package = "MungeSumstats")
formatted_path <- tempfile(fileext = "_eduAttainOkbay_standardised.tsv.gz")
dat <- MungeSumstats::read_sumstats(path = eduAttainOkbayPth, standardise_headers = TRUE)
formatted_path <- MungeSumstats::write_sumstats(sumstats_dt = dat, save_path = formatted_path, tabix_index = TRUE, write_vcf = FALSE, return_path = TRUE)
